target_customer: Engineering and test teams at battery, automotive, aerospace and electronics companies, including Fortune 100 firms
problem: Battery and hardware labs run experiments on specialized equipment and struggle to collect, clean and analyze test data. The company began as Byterat, software to automate battery lab data collection and analysis, and now sells agentic AI for hardware test programs.
business_model: Enterprise software, pricing not stated in sources opened
product_category: AI platform for hardware test data and engineering analysis

founders.name: Penelope Jones
education: University of Cambridge, PhD in Physics
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says she studied battery electrolytes as a doctoral student and programmed lab equipment, which led to the idea.

founders.name: Alpha Lee
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch calls him Jones's collaborator from graduate school and names him CSO; the YC page lists only Jones as a founder.

technical_complexity.rationale: Ingesting time series data from many lab instruments and modeling battery degradation is standard data engineering with hard domain modeling parts.

defensibility.rationale: Instrument integrations and accumulated test data create lock-in, but no external evidence of a data moat was opened.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent response found in sources opened.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in October 2023 describes industry battery scientists facing the same lab data problems Jones saw as a student. Battery development was expanding with EV demand.

branding.domain_note: Uses ohm.ai; earlier name Byterat used byterat.io.

identity.visual_style: enterprise tone with SOC 2 and ISO 27001 badges
identity.voice_and_tone: confident, forward-looking, short bold headlines such as 'Invent the future'

rebrands.why: Product broadened from battery data to hardware test programs; the reason is inferred from listings, not stated by the company

brand_strength.rationale: Short physical-units name that fits hardware, but a generic and confusable word with little press about the brand.

pivots.from: Battery lab data collection and analysis (Byterat)
pivots.to: Agentic AI platform for all hardware test programs (Ohm)
pivots.why: Broader market; reason inferred from company positioning, date not found

outcome_analysis: The company launched as Byterat, raised a $4M seed in October 2023 led by Giant Ventures, and later renamed to Ohm with a broader hardware test and AI agents pitch aimed at Fortune 100 engineering teams. It is active with a team of seven on the YC page. Growth evidence beyond positioning is thin, so the outcome is still open.
notes: Seed amount and investors come from a mirror of the TechCrunch article of 2023-10-27 and match a PitchBook snippet (27 Oct 2023, $4M, $4.5M total, unverified). CB Insights shows a $500K pre-seed in April 2023, unverified, not recorded. Founding year conflicts (2021, 2023, 2025). The YC page lists Penelope Jones only; Alpha Lee is CSO per TechCrunch. The YC page news link points to the Byterat article. No dated 2023 competitor named; Nominal appears only as a later adjacent company.
